input.summary: Move governing law to New York and replace mandatory arbitration with exclusive New York County court jurisdiction
input.comment: [Playbook] We have moved the governing law from Arizona to New York and replaced the mandatory arbitration mechanic with exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County (preserving temporary injunctive relief elsewhere), as our playbook requires an accepted governing law and a court forum. Delaware, California, or England and Wales with the courts of London would also be acceptable.

ops.oldText: the laws of the Arizona, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof.
ops.newText: the laws of the State of New York, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof.

ops.oldText: will be subject to and resolved by binding arbitration pursuant to the Arbitration Rules of U.S. Arbitration & Mediation, (www.usam.com). Any award or order rendered by the arbitrator may be confirmed as a judgment or order in any state or federal court of competent jurisdiction, which includes within the federal judicial district of the residence of the party against whom such award or order was entered.
ops.newText: will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York over the merits, and each party irrevocably submits to the jurisdiction of such courts; provided that either party may seek temporary injunctive relief in any other court of competent jurisdiction.
